overlays-dropdownmenu--default|light|ope: Radix hides the page behind an open menu with aria-hidden, and the hidden subtree still contains the menu's own trigger button. Investigated rather than accepted: with the menu open, four Tab presses in Chromium keep focus inside the portaled menu and never reach that button, and the page also carries pointer-events:none — so the focusable content inside the hidden subtree is not reachable while the menu is open, and no user can land on it. axe's aria-hidden-focus rule is structural and cannot see the primitive's focus management; it excuses exactly this shape for role=dialog (which is why the five dialog surfaces scan clean) and not for role=menu. The element it names, #storybook-root, is the story harness standing in for an app root. Upstream behaviour, not ours and not fixable from the wrapper: the only lever would be forking Radix's focus containment. ContextMenu has the same structure and is not reported only because its trigger is a span that cannot hold focus. Revisit if Radix adopts `inert`, which would make the subtree genuinely unreachable and satisfy the rule.
overlays-dropdownmenu--default|dark|open: Same finding as the light-theme entry above; the rule is structural and theme-independent, and both are listed so neither can disappear without the run noticing.
form-inputs-inputgroup--entry-states|lig: The one node is the "https://" addon of the disabled InputGroup in EntryStates. The field's input is disabled, so the whole group takes --opacity-disabled like a disabled Input, and the addon text dims with it. WCAG 1.4.3 exempts text that is part of an inactive user interface component; axe exempts it only for text inside a disabled form control, and the addon is a sibling span, so it cannot see that this text belongs to the disabled field. Dimming the addon is deliberate: a disabled field whose prefix stayed at full strength would read as half-enabled. Checked in Chromium (axe 2:1, #b7b7b7 on white); the enabled rows of the same story pass.
form-inputs-inputgroup--entry-states|dar: Same finding as the light-theme entry above: the disabled InputGroup's addon text, dimmed with its inactive field. Both are listed so neither can disappear without the run noticing.
